title: An overridden object's validation message never takes its .custom pair's translation, while the object's labels do
body:
domain:spec#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzfgvGexKn9vLHsy89K

Filing gate: ③ an accepted deviation of #30193 (PR #30236), carried as a follow-up; contract review 6648581045, should-fix 2. ⛔ Not a claim. Suggested-grade: p3, because it is visible only on an overridden object whose `.custom` pair ships its own translation of a validation message, and nothing is served with a pair input until #30062 lands. Route: `domain:spec` (resolver) together with objectql.

**What a user sees.** Once #30062 passes `pairBundle`, an overridden object's labels follow the ruled order (the pair's translation, then the override's own text, then the base's translation). Its `validations[].message` does not. A message the override reworded never takes the pair's translation. A message it left alone reads the merged catalog, where the pair's translation can lose to the base's by merge order (`packages/services/service-i18n/src/file-i18n-adapter.ts:189` deep-merges every package; `readAuthoredTranslationLayer` merges authored rows by item name).

**Why it was left.** `translateObjectValidations` stays on the plain merged bundle because the objectql rule evaluator (`packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts:3785`) answers the same message from `i18n.t()` with no pair input, and the pinned invariant is refusal text = served text. Moving only the resolver would break that invariant.

## Wanted

- [ ] Give the rule evaluator the same pair input the resolver gets (the override's `packagedBase` and its pair's own translations), and move `translateObjectValidations` and the evaluator onto the `labelCatalogs` / `catalogFor` rule together.
- [ ] Pin refusal text = served text on an overridden object with a pair translation, for a reworded and an unchanged message.

Blocked-by: #30062
Part-of: #30193
